text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, and through 23 games in Seattle this year he has three. He hasn't scored in 16 straight, and his 5.6% shooting is less than half what our talent range expects from him.

The good news for Seattle is that he's still doing the part he controls. He has 54 shots, 5.78 expected goals, and an individual chance rate (0.89 expected goals per 60) almost identical to last season's. Over his last ten games he's had 2.6 expected goals on his own shots, right at his usual level. That is the definition of a drought that should break.

The harder question is the five-on-five picture. Seattle has only 39.9% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is nearly eight points below his teammates. Last season Evolving-Hockey noted he faced the other team's best (97th percentile competition), which may be part of it again. He's fast, 95th percentile top speed by NHL EDGE, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 53% of his shots coming off the rush. Watch the shooting percentage first; the goals usually follow.
